name: Connecting Ridge C1 (illumination peak)
note: Ridge between Shackleton and de Gerlache craters; at 2 m above ground it averages 88.0% illumination with a longest shadow of 112 h (20 m LOLA map, hourly 2017–2037).
source_title: Gläser et al. 2018, Illumination conditions at the lunar poles: Implications for future exploration, PSS 162:170–178, Table 1 (NTRS author manuscript)

name: Shackleton rim S (illumination peak)
note: Shackleton rim peak: 81.0% average illumination at the surface, Sun at least partly visible 85.5% of the time, longest shadow 221 h (20 m LOLA map, hourly 2017–2037).
source_title: Gläser et al. 2018, Illumination conditions at the lunar poles: Implications for future exploration, PSS 162:170–178, Table 1 (NTRS author manuscript)

name: Shackleton crater (floor)
note: 21-km crater next to the south pole whose floor is permanently shadowed; IAU center point, a potential cold trap for water ice.
source_title: USGS/IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature: Shackleton

name: Peak near Shackleton (Bussey 2010 best point)
note: Approximate (±2–3 km; 474 m/px Kaguya map, single year): ridge off Shackleton's rim lit 86% of 2020, the best-lit point in that study.
source_title: Bussey et al. 2010, Illumination conditions of the south pole of the Moon derived using Kaguya topography, Icarus 208:558–564 (abstract)

name: Artemis III region: Peak near Cabeus B
note: Approximate region center (mean of 5 candidate landing sites in Table A1): a peak near Cabeus B crater.
source_title: Wueller et al. 2026, JGR Planets 131, e2025JE009434, Table A1 (regions per NASA Oct 2024 list)

name: Artemis III region: Haworth
note: Approximate region center (mean of 11 candidate landing sites in Table A1): near the rims of Haworth and Cabeus craters.
source_title: Wueller et al. 2026, JGR Planets 131, e2025JE009434, Table A1 (regions per NASA Oct 2024 list)

name: Artemis III region: Malapert Massif

name: Artemis III region: Mons Mouton Plateau

name: Artemis III region: Mons Mouton

name: Artemis III region: Nobile Rim 1
note: Approximate region center (mean of 9 candidate landing sites in Table A1): on Mons Mouton near the western rim of Nobile crater.

name: IM-1 Odysseus (Intuitive Machines)
note: Nova-C lander that touched down 22 Feb 2024 near Malapert A and tipped over — the first US soft landing since 1972.
source_title: LROC: Intuitive Machines IM-1 On The Moon! (26 Feb 2024)

name: IM-2 Athena (Intuitive Machines)
note: Landed 6 Mar 2025 on Mons Mouton and came to rest on its side in a 20-m crater.
source_title: LROC: IM-2 Athena Seen Obliquely

name: VIPER planned mission area (Mons Mouton)
note: Center of the planned mission area for NASA's VIPER ice-prospecting rover, west of Nobile crater (not a landing point).
source_title: Heldmann et al. 2026, The Relevance of the VIPER Mission to NASA's Artemis Human Exploration of the Moon, PSJ 7(4), doi:10.3847/PSJ/ae4232 (NTRS manuscript)

name: Chandrayaan-3 Vikram (Statio Shiv Shakti)
note: ISRO's Vikram lander and Pragyan rover touched down 23 Aug 2023, the southernmost landing at the time (outside our terrain coverage: smooth Moon).
source_title: LROC: Chandrayaan-3 Landing Site (5 Sep 2023)

name: Apollo 11 LM Eagle
note: First crewed Moon landing, 20 Jul 1969, in Mare Tranquillitatis.
source_title: LROC Coordinates of Lunar Anthropogenic Features, 28 Jul 2016 (basis of Wagner et al. 2017, Icarus 283)

name: Apollo 12 LM Intrepid
note: Pinpoint landing 19 Nov 1969 in Oceanus Procellarum, beside the Surveyor 3 probe.
source_title: LROC Coordinates of Lunar Anthropogenic Features, 28 Jul 2016 (basis of Wagner et al. 2017, Icarus 283)

name: Apollo 14 LM Antares
note: Landed 5 Feb 1971 in the Fra Mauro highlands, Apollo 13's original target.
source_title: LROC Coordinates of Lunar Anthropogenic Features, 28 Jul 2016 (basis of Wagner et al. 2017, Icarus 283)

name: Apollo 15 LM Falcon
note: Landed 30 Jul 1971 at Hadley–Apennine; first mission with the Lunar Roving Vehicle.
source_title: LROC Coordinates of Lunar Anthropogenic Features, 28 Jul 2016 (basis of Wagner et al. 2017, Icarus 283)

name: Apollo 16 LM Orion
note: Landed 21 Apr 1972 in the Descartes highlands.
source_title: LROC Coordinates of Lunar Anthropogenic Features, 28 Jul 2016 (basis of Wagner et al. 2017, Icarus 283)

name: Apollo 17 LM Challenger
note: Last crewed landing, 11 Dec 1972, in the Taurus–Littrow valley.
source_title: LROC Coordinates of Lunar Anthropogenic Features, 28 Jul 2016 (basis of Wagner et al. 2017, Icarus 283)

name: Chang'e 3 (with Yutu rover)
note: China's first lunar landing, 14 Dec 2013, in northern Mare Imbrium.
source_title: LROC Coordinates of Lunar Anthropogenic Features, 28 Jul 2016 (basis of Wagner et al. 2017, Icarus 283)

name: Chang'e 5
note: China's sample-return lander (1 Dec 2020) near Mons Rümker in northern Oceanus Procellarum.
source_title: LROC: First Look: Chang'e 5 (4 Dec 2020)

name: SLIM (JAXA)
note: Japan's pinpoint-landing demonstrator, which touched down 19 Jan 2024 on the slope of Shioli crater.
source_title: LROC: JAXA SLIM Landing (26 Jan 2024)

name: Blue Ghost Mission 1 (Firefly)
note: Firefly's commercial lander, which landed upright 2 Mar 2025 in Mare Crisium near Mons Latreille.
source_title: LROC: Blue Ghost Lunar Lander Seen From Above (7 Mar 2025)

name: Chang'e 4 (with Yutu-2 rover)
note: First soft landing on the far side, 3 Jan 2019, on the floor of Von Kármán crater in the South Pole–Aitken basin.

name: Chang'e 6
note: First far-side sample return, landed 1 Jun 2024 (UTC) in the southern Apollo basin.
